key: The Tao produced One; One produced Two; Two produced Three; Three produced All things.
s: Before turning to kings and their humble titles, the chapter opens on a sequence of births; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 42, takes the Two as yin and yang, and the Three as harmonious, clear and turbid breaths that become heaven, earth and man.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 42, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 1552800 (2019)

evidence.words: 陰陽生和、清、濁三氣，分為天地人也。
evidence.gloss: Yin and yang produce three breaths, the harmonious, the clear and the turbid, which divide to become heaven, earth and man.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 42, at [41]). Packet.js names revision 1552800 for chapter 42, as cited. The Heshang Gong commentary on 一生二 gives 一生陰與陽也 (the One produces yin and yang: the Two) and on 二生三 gives the quoted words (yin and yang produce the harmonious, clear and turbid breaths, which divide into heaven, earth and man: the Three). The line commented on matches Legge’s chapter. Plain sense faithful, no four-word run from the verse. Entry-check ok.
